title: Parametric study on the effect of power-to-volume ratio on long-term core cooling during small-break loss-of-coolant accidents in compact integral pressurized water reactors
abstract: Small-modular reactors (SMRs) are alternatives to conventional large nuclear power plants. Consequently, their design characteristics and safety must be optimized. Herein, the effects of reactor vessel volume and core power on small-break loss-of-coolant accident (SBLOCA) in integral pressurized water reactor (iPWR)-type SMRs were investigated using the MARS-KS system code. A 3×3 parametric matrix was developed by varying the vessel volume (1:1, 1:2, and 1:4/3 scale) and core power (80, 160, and 240 MWt) under controlled passive safety system conditions. Governing mechanisms divided the transient into discharge-dominant and long-term cooling phases. During the discharge-dominant phase, the discharged coolant mass scales with the vessel volume (51–52% and 75–76% of the baseline discharged mass), whereas the resulting water-level reduction follows a cube-root dependence on the volume due to geometric scaling effects (81% and 91–92% of the baseline level drop). During the long-term cooling phase, the collapsed water-level change rate exhibits a linear correlation with the power-to-volume ratio (q/V). Therefore, the reactor compactness influences SBLOCA performance through two mechanisms: the volume determines the coolant inventory remaining after blowdown, whereas q/V governs the long-term cooling behavior. This work quantifies the compactness penalty that a later PSS sizing must compensate for SMRs.

title: Evaluation of the shutdown capability of a soluble boron-free small modular reactor by PRAGMA
abstract: ABSTRACT Soluble boron-free (SBF) cores exhibit a strongly negative moderator temperature coefficient, inserting a large positive reactivity during overcooling events. Without soluble boron, the control element assemblies (CEAs) alone must hold the core subcritical throughout the post-trip cooldown, making the shutdown margin (SDM) after complete rod insertion the key measure of shutdown capability. This study evaluates the SDM of the SBF BANDI-60 core with the GPU-based Monte Carlo code PRAGMA. Among the uniform and asymmetric cooldowns investigated in static calculations, the uniform cold zero power (CZP) state at the beginning of cycle (BOC) is limiting. The SDM at this state is evaluated in two frameworks: the reactivity balance of conventional PWRs and the direct evaluation of the effective multiplication factor ( ) as in boiling water reactors (BWRs), whose shutdown function the CEAs serve. The directly evaluated is 0.9819, an SDM of 1.85% , satisfying the reference acceptance criterion < 0.99 in a nominal comparison; the reactivity balance falls short of the criterion only through its 10% scram-worth allowance, a PWR uncertainty convention. CEA depletion reduces the SDM by at most 0.12% over three cycles but drives the B-10 depletion of the regulating group's bottom quarter to 32% within one cycle.
title_ko: 프라그마에 의한 가용성 무붕소 소형모듈원자로(SMR)의 셧다운 능력 평가

title: Are non-invasive tube voltage measurements sufficiently accurate for establishing reference X-ray fields for calibration of radiation protection dosimeters?
abstract: Radiation protection calibrations are performed in reference radiation fields established according to ISO 4037-1 standard. Accurate X-ray tube voltage measurements are necessary for X-ray radiation qualities, because many relevant parameters, most importantly, conversion coefficients from air kerma to operational quantities, depend on tube voltage. The standard requires invasive measurements using a calibrated voltage divider, but this requires significant additional investments and is relatively complicated. Other, non-invasive, methods exist, but they are not recommended by the standard. In this paper, the invasive and non-invasive methods are compared and their uncertainty budgets are analyzed. Tube voltage range between 40 kV and 150 kV was investigated. Comparison between different methods is excellent within the reported uncertainties, with only 2 non-conforming results, out of 91. The results show that non-invasive methods, such as linear extrapolation by spectrometry, spectrometric practical endpoint, and X-ray multimeters can be used to achieve the measurement uncertainties that meet the requirements for most of standard X-ray radiation qualities, which makes them a viable alternative to voltage dividers.

title: An economic assessment of naval nuclear fuel reprocessing for HALEU production: A public-private partnership model
abstract: The United States faces a growing demand for High-Assay Low Enriched Uranium (HALEU) to support nuclear innovation and energy security. This work explores the feasibility of reprocessing and down-blending used naval nuclear fuel to create a supply of HALEU to decrease government liability while increasing nuclear innovation within the United States. Several nations successfully reprocess commercial spent nuclear fuel, and historically, the Department of Energy has also done so. The potential revenue of this project, at projected market costs, could supply operational costs for the government. Drawbacks lie in the capital costs of such a facility and the likely need to implement unproven technology. Ultimately, the reprocessing of Naval nuclear fuel presents a unique opportunity for the United States to reduce significant liabilities and invest in the country's energy future.

title: The effect of chromium equivalent on the microstructure and mechanical properties of weld metal for SIMP steels
abstract: SIMP steel is a low-activation ferritic/martensitic alloy containing approximately 9–12 wt.% Cr, which has attracted increasing interest for core components in lead-cooled fast reactors. However, its engineering application is limited by the lack of specialized low-activation welding wires. In this study, three low-activation welding wires with different chromium equivalents (Cr eq ) were designed and fabricated based on low-activation alloy design principles. The effects of Cr eq variation on δ-ferrite retention, microstructural characteristics, and mechanical behavior of the weld metals were systematically investigated. The results indicate that reducing Cr eq effectively suppresses δ-ferrite formation. When Cr eq was decreased to 8.276, the weld metal exhibited an almost fully martensitic microstructure. In addition, the multilayer multi-pass welding process promoted the elimination of δ-ferrite in the weld metal. Increasing δ-ferrite content led to reductions in hardness, strength, and high-temperature elongation, whereas no clear change in room-temperature elongation was observed. Among the welding wires studied, the W3 welding wire with Creq of 8.276 not only meets the low activation requirement but also has an impact energy of 68 J, a room-temperature tensile strength of 790 MPa, and a tensile strength of 430 MPa at 550°C. These findings provide valuable guidance for developing dedicated welding consumables for low-activation ferritic/martensitic steels.
title_ko: SIMP강용 용접금속의 미세조직 및 기계적 특성에 미치는 크롬 당량의 영향

title: Rapid spatiotemporal prediction of radionuclide dispersion in complex environments based on a lightweight UNet-Transformer
abstract: Accidental radionuclide release during spent nuclear fuel transportation may pose serious risks to public health and environmental safety, requiring rapid and accurate dispersion prediction for emergency response. However, lightweight prediction frameworks for complex roadside environments containing buildings and vegetation remain insufficiently explored. This study proposes a lightweight spatiotemporal framework integrating a depthwise separable convolution UNet with dual Transformer modules. Spatial and temporal Transformers capture multiscale spatial features and long-range dispersion evolution, while conditional feature encoding improves adaptability under varying environmental conditions. A residual prediction strategy and lightweight refinement module further enhance autoregressive stability and concentration reconstruction. The model is evaluated using CFD-generated datasets covering different wind speeds, vegetation resistance coefficients, and release intensities. Results show that the proposed framework reduces MAE, RMSE, and inference time by approximately 67%, 53%, and 32%, respectively, compared with the conventional UNet-Transformer, and by 42%, 24%, and 41% compared with the lightweight UNet-ConvLSTM. Furthermore, cumulative inhalation dose distributions reconstructed from predicted concentration fields yield an average relative dose prediction error of approximately 1.13% across two testing scenarios, demonstrating the framework's potential for rapid radiological consequence assessment and nuclear emergency decision support.

title: Defining Axial Void Fraction and Flashing Details from Pressure Profiles in Two-Phase Critical Flow Discharges Made in CRAFTY Facility
abstract: This article focuses on defining an axial void fraction from axial pressure and temperature measurements in two-phase critical flow discharges made with CriticAl Flow Test facility (CRAFTY), a separate-effect-test facility located in Lappeenranta-Lahti University of Technology in Lappeenranta, Finland. Additionally, a method to approximate the flashing delay from the same axial pressure profiles is included. The discharge tube (DT) in CRAFTY resembles the VVER-440 steam generator tube with an inner diameter of 13 mm and has a length-to-diameter (L/D) ratio of 350 for the used cases. In the paper, various tests from a test-matrix conducted in 2024 are used for analysis. The tests range from high subcooling case (ΔTsub ~ 60°C, pup ~ 8 MPa) to near saturation case (ΔTsub ~ 5°C, pup ~ 5 MPa). The flashing delay was defined for low subcooling tests only as the flashing in the high subcooling occurs at the outlet and is nearly instant when assuming that a single-phase subcooled liquid is affected only by friction pressure loss in linear fashion. The flashing delay is defined as the time between when the inlet saturation pressure is reached to inception of higher two-phase pressure loss. This is done with the means of line fitting from the axial pressure measurements. Essentially, it is assumed that after the liquid reaches the inlet saturation pressure it goes to a metastable state before flashing occurs and voiding starts axially, which can be detected from the axial pressure profile of the DT. The axial pressure profiles can offer insights where the continuous liquid phase disperses into non-continuous mist/droplet flow. At this location lies the two-phase choke plane as the pressure information from downstream cannot travel upward into upstream anymore. The two-phase sonic velocities are an order of magnitude lower than either the liquid or gas phase. In one-phase critical flow, the flow velocity reaches Mach 1, making the pressure signal stalled, not able to travel upstream. For two-phase critical flow, this analogy is not correct.

title: Comparing Fuel Homogenization Strategies for an OpenMC Depletion Analysis of a TRISO-Fueled, Helium-Cooled Microreactor
abstract: Many advanced reactor designs incorporate TRISO fuel, as it combines excellent safety and fuel performance characteristics. While the small particulate design provides benefits, the sheer number of fuel particles per reactor poses significant challenges for high-fidelity simulation. This work tests various homogenization strategies against a fully explicit TRISO depletion model by computing the difference in k-eigenvalue for an infinite assembly of a helium-cooled microreactor. Two partial homogenization strategies, named kernel-only and two-layer, were investigated along with a naive volume homogenization. The aim of the partial homogenizations is to save memory and runtime while retaining sufficient accuracy—when compared to the explicit case—for use in a full-core model. The simulations use OpenMC for Monte Carlo neutron transport and depletion. In the end, both of the partial homogenizations were able to produce statistically similar results to the explicit case with k-eigenvalue 2σ confidence intervals largely overlapping for all depletion steps. The full homogenization k-eigenvalues were expectedly lower than the explicit case, with Δρ confidence interval means starting near 1400 pcm at beginning-of-life increasing to near 2200 pcm at the highest burnup computed (~47 GWd/tonne-U). The memory and runtime savings were less promising, saving about 8% total memory (110 GB) and ~10 h or 26 880 cpu-hours (24 MPI processes, 112 theads per process). While the savings would help in a full-core model, there is more room for work that reduces TRISO computing requirements.
title_ko: TRISO 연료, 헬륨 냉각 초소형원자로의 OpenMC 연소 분석을 위한 연료 균질화 전략 비교

title: MCGeoBridge: A bounded semantics-preserving method for MCNP-to-GDML geometry transfer
abstract: MCNP-to-Geant4 geometry reuse is difficult because MCNP defines regions by Boolean combinations of oriented surfaces, whereas GDML requires finite solids in a volume hierarchy. This work presents MCGeoBridge, a method that preserves MCNP cell-expression membership within a declared finite domain while emitting standard Geant4 GDML. It uses abstract-syntax-tree parsing, conservative normalization of supported complements, exact primitive recovery for reducible boxes, cylinders, and spheres, and bounded Boolean lowering of other surface-defined leaves. Validation combines language-coverage accounting with source-expression, converted-solid, and independent Geant4 point-classification checks. Across nine regression models and 420 resolved cells, 193,318 global, cell-local, and boundary-directed points produced no disagreement with source classification in either the internal evaluator or Geant4; 390 of 420 cells had discriminating samples under the stated protocol. A geometry-deduplicated corpus of 70 medium-complexity decks generated well-formed GDML with valid internal references; approximation status, warnings, and source-material completeness are reported separately. Destination loading and navigation checks assess expanded lattice cases. These results support per-cell geometry agreement for tested supported cases within the declared finite conversion domain.
title_ko: MCGeoBridge: MCNP-GDML 지오메트리 전송을 위한 제한된 의미론 보존 방법

title: Joint Fault Diagnosis of Nuclear Main Pump Sliding Bearings Under Variable Operating Conditions Using Multi-Task 2D Residual Network
abstract: : Monitoring sliding bearings in nuclear reactor coolant pumps is challenging because variable-frequency noise masks weak early-stage faults, and traditional 1D deep learning models suffer from "feature over-smoothing". To address this, we propose a joint diagnosis framework based on a Multi-task Two-dimensional Residual Network (MT-2D-ResNet). A spatiotemporal phase trajectory folding mechanism transforms multi-channel time-series signals into 2D topological matrices, achieving spatial alignment between macroscopic periodicity and microscopic transient impacts. Additionally, an auxiliary speed prediction branch is introduced to dynamically decouple variable-frequency environmental noise. Results demonstrate that a streamlined network without redundant attention pooling optimally retains high-frequency impact characteristics. Experimental validation on a simulated bearing-rotor test bench shows the model achieving a highly robust mean fault classification accuracy of 94.0% across five fault categories and three evolution stages under severe variable-frequency conditions (1000–6000 r/min). Ultimately, this framework provides a reliable intelligent diagnostic solution for the predictive maintenance of critical rotating equipment in the nuclear industry.
title_ko: 다중 작업 2D 잔류 네트워크를 사용하여 가변 작동 조건 하에서 원자력 메인 펌프 슬라이딩 베어링의 조인트 결함 진단

title: Hybrid Genetic Algorithm with a GNN-Based Surrogate Model for Pipe Support Design Optimization in Nuclear Power Plant
abstract: Pipe support design for nuclear power plant piping systems is traditionally performed through iterative piping stress analyses based on engineering experience, requiring significant time and effort. This study proposes a hybrid optimization framework combining a Genetic Algorithm (GA), a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based surrogate model, and PIPESTRESS analysis for pipe support optimization. Support types were defined as design variables, while ASME Code stress ratios were used as design constraints. GA optimization successfully reduced the number of supports while maintaining acceptable stress-ratio levels. To reduce the computational cost of repeated PIPESTRESS analyses, a GNN surrogate model was developed using graph representations of piping geometries and support configurations. A dataset consisting of 3,600 samples from three piping geometries was used for training and validation. The surrogate model was developed to evaluate unseen support configurations within predefined piping geometries rather than arbitrary unseen piping layouts. Although the surrogate model showed good overall prediction performance, lower accuracy was observed for some evaluation criteria, and these prediction errors affected the optimization results when the GNN was used alone. To improve optimization reliability, a hybrid approach was introduced in which all candidates were evaluated by the GNN and selected candidates were reanalyzed using PIPESTRESS. The proposed method reduced computational time by 36.0–59.7% while maintaining support configurations and stress-ratio levels comparable to those obtained using conventional PIPESTRESS-based optimization.

title: Alkali-Activated Solidification of Spent Zeolite Adsorbents: Compaction, Volume Reduction, and Waste Form Performance
abstract: This study developed a compaction-assisted solidification process for spent zeolite adsorbents from a heavy-water reactor using an alkali-activated zeolite (AAZ) waste form. The AAZ waste form was prepared by mixing zeolite with an alkaline activator composed of sodium silicate and sodium hydroxide, followed by uniaxial compaction at 10 MPa. The effects of initial curing temperature, NaOH concentration, and sodium silicate-to-sodium hydroxide solution mass ratio (SS/SH ratio) were evaluated based on compressive strength. The highest-strength AAZ waste form was further evaluated for thermal-cycling stability and leachability. The highest mean compressive strength of 14.88 MPa was obtained using 10 M NaOH, an SS/SH ratio of 1.5, and initial 1-day curing at 60 °C followed by curing at room temperature (RT) for 27 days. After 30 thermal cycles between −40 and 60 °C, the specimens retained their structural integrity, with the compressive strength increasing from 14.88 to 17.53 MPa, indicating no apparent strength degradation. The leachability indices for stable Cs, Sr, and Co were 10.71, 13.73, and 12.28, respectively. Compaction reduced the specimen volume by 7.06% at a zeolite loading of 76 wt%. Overall, this study demonstrated the applicability of AAZ waste forms for high-loading solidification of spent zeolite adsorbents.

title: Thermal Neutron Scattering in Zirconium Hydride: Comparison of NJOY, CINEL, NCrystal, and ACEMAKER Processing Approaches
abstract: The accurate prediction of neutron moderation and transport in thermal reactor systems relies on reliable thermal neutron scattering data derived from the thermal scattering law S(α,β). In this work, we generated thermal scattering data for Monte Carlo codes in ENDF-6 format using three nuclear data processing tools, NJOY (LEAPR), CINEL, and NCrystal, while employing an identical phonon density of states as input, thereby isolating the impact of the data processing methodology and associated physical approximations. The resulting ENDF-6 data were subsequently converted into ACE format using NJOY for application in Monte Carlo simulations.The comparison shows very good agreement for the inelastic scattering component, while the differences in the elastic cross sections arise from the explicit treatment of coherent elastic scattering in CINEL and NCrystal. The resulting cross sections are applied to selected International Criticality Safety Benchmark Evaluation Project benchmark configurations to assess how the differences in data processing propagate to benchmark reactivity. In addition, the impact of nuclear data processing on the Monte Carlo results is investigated by converting identical ENDF-6 data into ACE format using both NJOY (ACER) and ACEMAKER, enabling a direct assessment of the effect of independent processing routes on benchmark reactivity.The results show that while the differences between the thermal scattering models have a limited impact on the benchmark responses, the ACE processing stage can introduce system-dependent reactivity variations of up to approximately 300 pcm for the benchmark cases and processing grids considered in this study, primarily due to differences in the incident energy grid and the interpolation of secondary energy distributions.
title_ko: 지르코늄 하이드라이드의 열 중성자 산란: NJOY, CINEL, NCrystal 및 ACEMAKER 처리 접근법 비교

title: Consent and Its Costs: Native American Tribes, the Nuclear Waste Negotiator, and the Limits of Voluntary Siting, 1990–1995
abstract: This paper traces the historical development of voluntary-based nuclear waste siting in the United States during the 1980s and 1990s. It draws on primary sources including the official records of the Office of the Nuclear Waste Negotiator; archival repositories in Utah, New Mexico, and Nevada; newspapers; and oral history. It argues that voluntary siting, far from offering a neutral participatory framework, systematically displaced the costs of federal credibility onto Native American Tribes. Focusing on negotiations between the ONWN and several Native American Tribes from 1990 to 1995, principally the Mescalero Apache Tribe and Skull Valley Band of Goshute, this paper critically examines the federal effort to develop monitored retrievable storage sites, revealing four key factors underpinning the program’s failure. This analysis provides crucial context for contemporary efforts in consent-based siting for the back-end nuclear fuel cycle.

title: Physics-informed deep generative model for longitudinal phase space reconstruction during beam merging at HIAF
abstract: Real-time longitudinal phase space (LPS) diagnostics are crucial for the highly dynamic beam merging process at HIAF. However, tracking the 2D LPS from a single 1D Wall Current Monitor (WCM) profile is a severely ill-posed problem, rendering traditional multi-turn tomography inapplicable. While standard deep learning accelerates 1D-to-2D inferences, it often generates non-physical artifacts. To address this, we propose P 2 -CVAE, a physics-informed generative model integrating perceptual loss with a charge-conservation projection penalty. This dual-constraint strategy restricts reconstructions to a physically valid manifold. Validation against numerical simulations demonstrates high geometric fidelity, achieving a PSNR of 34.62 dB and an IoU of 0.80, while consistently tracking macroscopic emittance expansion. Furthermore, experimental tests using raw WCM readouts confirm its operational readiness, maintaining a profile tracking correlation above 95% ( R > 0.95 ). With an inference latency under 3 ms, P 2 -CVAE provides a highly reliable, physics-aware solution for single-shot diagnostics.

title: Derivation of occupational accident risk during nuclear power plant decommissioning
abstract: During the decommissioning phase of nuclear power plants, workers may be exposed to both radiological and non-radiological effects resulting from occupational accidents, requiring a safety assessment during the decommissioning planning stage. This study derived risk levels by comprehensively considering both impacts of occupational accidents that may occur during NPP decommissioning. Occupational accidents that may occur during decommissioning were identified. And non-radiological risks were derived using a risk matrix based on construction-industry occupational accident statistics provided by the Ministry of Employment and Labor in Korea, collected over a 10-year period from 2015 to 2024. Worker exposure scenarios linked to these accidents were established to assess additional radiological impacts, which were then combined with the non-radiological risks to derive the final risk levels. The non-radiological risk levels ranged from 8 to 12(out of a maximum of 25), showing similar results across all occupational accident types. Among the radiation dose results, the explosion accident during stainless steel cutting yielded the highest value at 0.54 mSv, while the collapse accident during stainless steel cutting and fire accidents during waste handling recorded negligibly low values of 1 μSv. Fire, explosion, and collapse accidents were commonly rated as high-risk across all decommissioning processes, as these events can cause additional radiological impacts beyond non-radiological hazards. The findings of this study can be utilized in safety assessments for future decommissioning planning.

title: Assessment of Bubble Dynamics in Nucleate Boiling of Water Under High-Pressure Conditions
abstract: The wall heat flux in the nucleate boiling regime is governed by a small set of coupled bubble dynamics parameters, like the active nucleation site density, the bubble departure and lift-off diameters, the bubble growth rate, the growth and waiting periods, and the bubble departure frequency. In modern mechanistic heat flux partitioning frameworks of the type embedded in reactor subchannel and computational fluid dynamics codes, these quantities enter directly as closure relations, so the fidelity of any two-phase thermal-hydraulic prediction is limited by the fidelity of the underlying bubble dynamics correlations.This research work reviews the experimental data, correlations, and mechanistic models for each of these parameters, with two deliberate points of emphasis motivated by a pressurized heavy water reactor (PHWR) safety analysis: water as the working fluid, and the effect of system pressure.Foundational correlations from the literature (Fritz, Cole and Rohsenow, Hsu, Mikic, Rohsenow and Griffith, Kocamustafaogullari and Ishii, and Hibiki and Ishii) are compiled alongside recent experimental, numerical, and data-driven contributions, and are compared directly against the available high-pressure experimental data for water, including the high-resolution measurements of Kossolapov et al. and the high-pressure pool boiling data of Sakashita. Using saturation properties from the IAPWS-IF97 formulation of the International Association for the Properties of Water and Steam (IAPWS), the competing pressure trends are quantified for saturated water between 0.1 and 16 MPa: the bubble departure diameter and growth constant fall by roughly two orders of magnitude as pressure rises to reactor conditions, whereas the active nucleation site density rises by about three orders of magnitude and the departure frequency by about one.These opposing trends, together with recent high-resolution evidence that the vapor microlayer may be absent above 1 MPa, explain why correlations anchored at atmospheric pressure cannot be extrapolated to PHWR conditions and why mechanistic closures must be reexamined at high pressure.Finally, the specific situation of heavy water (D2O) is addressed. No dedicated D2O bubble dynamics measurements exist, and current practice substitutes light water correlations with D2O properties, a procedure justified by fluid-to-fluid scaling but as yet unvalidated. Priority research directions for PHWR-relevant bubble dynamics are identified. In particular, it is emphasized that at reactor conditions, the departure diameter and the ebullition time are distributions rather than single values, and that characterizing these distributions is a priority for PHWR-relevant analysis.

title: Microstructure-controlled aqueous dissolution of multi-dopant UO2 SIMFUEL across sintering and leaching conditions
abstract: Multi-element-doped UO 2 SIMFUEL pellets were fabricated by high-pressure compaction and sintering at 1550–1700 °C under a reducing atmosphere to simulate chemically complex, high-burnup-equivalent fuel compositions. SEM, XRD, EDS, and ICP-MS characterization revealed pronounced microstructural evolution with increasing sintering temperature. Sintering at 1700 °C promoted substantial grain coarsening and densification up to 96.3% theoretical density, reducing interconnected porosity and effective grain boundary area relative to pellets sintered at 1550 °C. This microstructural stabilization enhanced resistance to aqueous dissolution during one-year semi-dynamic leaching tests conducted at 25–90 °C in accordance with the ASTM C1308 protocol. Dopants partitioned into chemically resilient metallic ε-type phases and more soluble dopant-bearing oxide regions, giving rise to element-specific dissolution kinetics governed by phase chemistry and microstructural connectivity. Mo release reflected both normalization artifacts and genuinely faster dissolution at lower burnup. Beyond compositional effects, elevated leaching temperatures consistently accelerated elemental release and were accompanied by subtle lattice contraction, consistent with partial oxidation of the fluorite matrix. Collectively, these processing–microstructure–dissolution relationships provide mechanistic insights for improving the chemical durability of multi-component fluorite-structured nuclear fuels in aqueous environments.

title: A New Approach to Neutron Absorber Design for Criticality Safety of LEU+ Spent Fuel Pool
abstract: Increasing fuel enrichment to 5–10 wt.% (LEU+) is required for extending operating fuel cycles of nuclear power plants. However, the elevated reactivity of LEU+ fuel challenges the criticality management of the spent fuel pool, where conventional plate-type B 4 C/Al absorbers have been utilized. This study proposes an exploratory criticality control strategy that maintains the existing rack configuration for Region I in AP1000 by accommodating rod-type absorbers in the vacant control rod guide tubes. Using MCNP 6.3, candidate absorber materials (Gd 2 O 3 , Eu 2 O 3 , Sm 2 O 3 , Dy 2 O 3 , HfO 2 , SS304) were evaluated as plate-type and rod-type configurations under both unborated and borated water conditions. Proposed plate-type absorbers showed no improvement over the conventional B 4 C/Al absorbers. In contrast, SS304 rod-type absorbers inserted into the existing vacant guide tubes maintained subcriticality up to 9 wt.%, while the 10 wt.% case exceeded the subcriticality limit. B 4 C/Al rod absorbers satisfied the subcriticality criteria at enrichments up to 10 wt.%. These findings indicate that the rod-type SS304 absorbers inserted into guide tube positions can be a cost-effective solution for the safe storage of LEU+ spent fuels in wet pools.

title: Comprehensive characterization of powder ceramic waste: Implications for TENORM risk assessment and radiation protection
abstract: The structural and compositional characteristics of the powder ceramic waste were investigated using XRF, FTIR, XRD, and SEM–EDS analyses, confirming a highly crystalline structure, the characteristic ZrSiO 4 tetrahedral vibrations, and a homogeneous elemental distribution dominated by ZrO 2 and SiO 2 . The radiological assessment indicated activity concentrations of 238 U (2429±100.6 Bq.kg -1 ), 226 Ra (2527±86 Bq.kg -1 ), 232 Th (513.3±48.7 Bq.kg -1 ), and 40 K (193.14 ±13.5 Bq.kg -1 ). The calculated radiological hazard indices exhibited relatively high values, including radium equivalent activity (3278 ±155 Bq.kg -1 ), absorbed dose rate (1488±69 nGy.h -1 ), and annual effective dose (1.8±0.1 mSv.y -1 ), all of which were substantially higher than the corresponding internationally recommended reference values. Additional radiological indicators further demonstrated the elevated radiological characteristics of the investigated waste and highlighted the need for appropriate radiation protection and waste management measures. These findings are primarily attributed to the elevated activity concentrations of Naturally Occurring Radioactive Materials (NORM) present in the investigated ceramic waste. Overall, the investigated zirconium silicate waste was classified as TENORM, emphasizing the need for appropriate regulatory control, radiological screening, radiation protection measures, and controlled waste management strategies to ensure its safe handling and potential reuse.

title: Data-driven prediction of eutectic MgCl2–KCl molten salt viscosity using advanced machine learning across 553–1346 K
abstract: Eutectic MgCl 2 –KCl (32:68 mol%) molten salt has attracted considerable interest in high-temperature energy applications, including thermal-energy storage and heat-transfer systems. Accurate viscosity prediction is important for optimal system design and operation. In this study, 1045 experimental viscosity data were compiled from the literature, cleaned and screened, resulting in 987 retained observations. Seven conventional viscosity correlations were first evaluated, followed by development of a comprehensive machine-learning framework for modelling viscosity as a function of temperature (553–1346 K) and density (1.46–2.12 g cm -3 ). The models developed in this study included multilayer perceptron (MLP), cascade-forward neural network (CFNN), Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH) and hard-monotonic physics-informed MLP (PI-MLP), with temperature-only and temperature–density inputs. The data-driven neural networks were trained using a range of gradient-based and evolutionary optimisation algorithms. A five-fold cross-validation (CV) process was applied to an 80% development set to select the optimal model, while the remaining 20% was reserved as an independent test set. The MLP-SCG (2-25-25-1) model achieved the lowest CV root mean square error, with test and total RMSE values of 0.779 and 0.603 cP, respectively. In contrast, dependency-aware leave-one-source-out (LOSO) validation indicated reduced generalisation to previously unseen literature sources. MLP-Adam and MLP-BR demonstrated greater robustness at the source level, underscoring the significance of source dependency in evaluating model transferability. The hard-monotonic PI-MLP models produced physically consistent, non-negative apparent activation energies in the liquid domain, with median values of 5.49 and 8.34 kJ mol -1 for the temperature-only and temperature–density formulations, respectively. Williams-plot analysis indicated that 93.91% of test observations were within the applicability domain of MLP-SCG. The proposed framework provides an efficient means of estimating MgCl 2 –KCl viscosity while also allowing predictive accuracy, source-level generalisation, and physical consistency to be assessed separately.

title: Introducing GAINS, a GPU-accelerated continuous energy CSG based neutron Monte Carlo simulation code
abstract: GAINS is a GPU-accelerated Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG)-based continuous energy Monte Carlo neutron simulation code, designed for full core optimization, with regard to criticality and neutronics reactor performance. GAINS combines a hybrid event-history workflow to curb warp divergence, replaces Probability Density Functions (PDFs) with precomputed Cumulative Distribution Functions (CDFs), direct-indexed data layouts, and unrolls recursive CSG traversal into a stack-based scheme, which is evaluated using a spherical ray-march algorithm. Additionally, GAINS incorporates a localized and customizable distance cache. Accuracy and performance are assessed on three problems: the PU-239 Jezebel critical benchmark, a cylindrical fuel-element case (Base) with a movable hafnium absorber, and a full-core lattice industry benchmark. GAINS reproduces reference trends with small, traceable biases k eff of 21 pcm (Jezebel), 40 pcm average across control-rod positions (Base), and 28 pcm (Benchmark), primarily attributable to resampling inaccuracies in cross-section data leading to a faster spectrum. On an RTX 4090, GAINS completes 136 million histories in 23.26 s (Base) and 271.48 s (Benchmark), achieving 47.2 × and 6.1 × speed-ups over Serpent 2 on a dual-Xeon (160-thread) node, with significantly better cost-to-performance. Enabling the cache increases these speed-ups to an overall speed-up of 57.6x - 8.2x, respectively. The resulting capability enables fast, accurate neutronics calculations suitable for optimization loops and rapid design iteration on commodity hardware, while maintaining agreement with CSG-based CPU codes.
